messages:
matt: Heads up — ran into a weird packaging/lock mismatch between my macbook dev env and CI today.
laura: ugh what happened?
matt: On mac (arm64) poetry.lock pulled a source package for my conditional dep, CI (linux amd64) ended up trying to install a wheel with cp310-cp310-manylinux tag and pip failed with a binary incompatible error.
samir: do you have the error snippet?
matt: sure, paste below:
```
ERROR: Package 'somelib' requires a different Python: 3.11.0 not in '>=3.10, <3.11'
Collecting somelib-1.2.3-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl
  ERROR: somelib-1.2.3-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform.
```
ivy: that sounds like poetry's lock was generated on a different platform/marker set. Did you run `poetry lock` on mac?
matt: yup. I thought lockfiles were platform-agnostic but env markers in pyproject with os_name and platform_machine are biting us. Example in pyproject: 
```
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
requests = "^2.31"
httpx = { version = "^0.25", optional = true }
async = { version = "^0.1", markers = "python_version >= \"3.10\" and sys_platform != \"win32\"" }
```
laura: ah the `markers` in editable/conditional extras. poetry will resolve differently depending on the machine where `poetry lock` is run.
samir: common pattern: dev on mac -> lock excludes some linux-only wheels and vice versa. CI must reproduce platform markers when exporting requirements.
matt: CI is just `poetry install --no-root` on linux runners. I think poetry exported a requirements.txt that referenced mac-only source packages and pip picked a linux wheel incompatible with our python version.
ivy: Workarounds we've used before: 1) run `poetry lock` inside the same platform as CI (use linux container locally) 2) use `poetry export --format requirements.txt --without-hashes --platform manylinux2014_x86_64` so the export resolves for the target platform.
laura: FYI `--platform` works only on recent poetry versions and you need `poetry-core` resolver support. Also `poetry export` can accept `--extras` to include optional deps consistently.
samir: Another pragmatic fix: remove platform-specific markers from pyproject and rely on runtime checks, or pin wheels for problematic deps. Not ideal but reduces surprise.
matt: Also ran into missing async extras: my local env had `httpx[http2]` installed via an extras group but CI lock didn't include it because of markers. At runtime we got: 
```
AttributeError: 'Client' object has no attribute 'stream_async'
```
ivy: That explains the runtime crash. For the async SDK bug report: ensure extras used by the async client are in `extras = ["async"]` and add a CI smoke test that imports the async client.
laura: For a durable solution we should: 
- standardize on lock generation in a linux container (org dev guide)
- add `poetry export --platform` step in CI for wheel/platform reproducibility
- add a small integration that exercises `redwood.async_client` so extras get validated
matt: Agreed. Also adding one-off command if someone needs to regenerate lock locally: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src -w /src python:3.11-slim bash -c "pip install poetry && poetry lock --no-update"`
samir: nice. For immediate unblock, I did `pip install --no-binary somelib` in CI and that allowed building from sdist which matched our python. Not great perf-wise but unblocks.
ivy: I'll open a tiny PR to the onboarding docs recommending "generate lock in linux" and add the CI export step.
laura: thanks. Also tagging devex-bot to remind folks when opening PRs that touch pyproject: :devex-bot: could we add a lint check for changes to pyproject to ensure `poetry.lock` regenerated?
devex-bot: Noted — creating issue #DEVEX-412: "enforce poetry.lock regen when pyproject changes" (automated).
matt: sweet. One more gotcha: if you use editable installs (`poetry install -e`) the editable metadata can hide missing extras. So CI non-editable installs catch missing deps earlier.
samir: good call. We should recommend non-editable installs in CI.
ivy: I'll add a short checklist in the PR: regenerate lock in linux, export with platform, non-editable CI install, add async import smoke test.
matt: thanks folks, saved my afternoon :) :thumbsup:
laura: :party_parrot:
